title: Preface
summary: A declassified JFK assassination records identification form (JCS 202-10001-10172, released 1998 under the JFK Records Act) for a 1962 24-page TOP SECRET memorandum on Operation Mongoose and "The Cuba Project," dated 01/18/62. It covers a program review by Brig. Gen. E. G. Lansdale, Chief of Operations, with deletions by CIA, State, and OSD, and some Joint Staff withholdings.

title: 1, OBJECTIVE

nodes.title: 1, OBJECTIVE (intro)
nodes.summary: U.S. objective: help Cubans overthrow the Communist regime from within and install a government the U.S. can live with peacefully. Concept: a Cuban popular revolt, generated and directed by a strongly motivated political action movement inside Cuba, supported by economic warfare, psychological operations, and sabotage/guerrilla groups. Notes the failed April 1961 operation undermined Cuban trust, so Latin American support and exposure of Soviet/Bloc interference are needed. The climactic revolt may be triggered by an angry popular reaction or a government action. Once begun, the movement seizes and holds areas, appeals to Western Hemisphere nations, and receives open U.S. support.

nodes.title: I. ESTIMATE OF THE SITUATION
nodes.summary: The text is an excerpt from a 1961 U.S. estimate of the situation regarding Cuba, dated 28 November. It states that planning requires sound intelligence estimates, notes an error in the latest National Estimate (SNIE 85-61) that contains operational conclusions not based on hard fact, and says the planning, based on the hard intelligence estimate of the situation, will be revised as necessary. It mentions a new National Intelligence Estimate (NIE 85-62) due 23 January, since postponed to 7 February, and recognizes that a result of the Project has been the collection of intelligence on Cuba in depth to establish firm facts for estimates and operations.

nodes.title: IV. INITIAL PHASE
key_items: A. Establish a U.S. mechanism for the project.
nodes.summary: A declassified 1961-62 CIA/U.S. government status report on the initial phase (30 Nov 1961 - 18 Jan 1962) of the Cuba project. It covers: establishing a U.S. operations mechanism under Gen. Lansdale and interagency representatives; intelligence support, including interrogation of Cuban refugees and agent buildup; developing a political platform and a nucleus of Cuban political action agents; deploying action groups in Havana and provinces; diplomatic efforts at the OAS foreign ministers meeting; economic warfare and sabotage options against Cuba's sugar economy, transport, and shipping; military contingency planning; special group operations via Church, labor, youth, and professional contacts; and a concluding outlook that CIA capabilities fall short of project goals.

nodes.title: V. TARGET SCHEDULE
A. Intelligence
nodes.summary: A sensitive target schedule with three intelligence tasks: (1) NIE 85-62 on Cuba due 7 February (CLA); (2) by 15 February, an effective interrogation/processing operation at Opa Locka Interrogation Center for collection, with support from Defense, State, I&NS, and FBI; (3) a CLA survey of the intelligence area, prioritized by refugee points (Cuban refugees, Puerto Rico, Venezuela, and other refugee points) and inside Cuba, including countries with diplomatic relations, with a capability report due 15 February to ensure maximum coverage of the target date.

nodes.title: B. Political
nodes.summary: A declassified 1960s US planning document lists tasks (Tasks 5-28) for toppling the Cuban Communist regime. Political: CIA defector and popular-movement plans, deception and covert operations, State/OAS follow-up. Economic: trade restrictions, shipping and port harassment, pressure on unions, shippers, NATO and Japan, and disrupting Cuban nickel and food crops. Psychological: USIA and CIA propaganda campaigns, symbols, and morale materials to build sympathy for Cuba and provoke internal uprising. Most deadlines fall in February.

nodes.title: E. Military Action
nodes.summary: Military action tasks for a Cuba project: Defense to submit by 28 Feb a contingency plan for U.S. military force supporting the Cuban popular movement, with conditions where action is required and unlikely to cause general war; CIA to submit by 15 Feb an operational schedule for sabotage inside Cuba tied to building a popular movement; CIA to request Defense support early, with major needs expected by 23 Feb; Defense to submit a special operations plan by 28 Feb. Future plans: by 20 Feb realistic task plans expected for a firm timetable. Notes that CIA's popular-movement framework may create a pretext for armed intervention, which conflicts with presidential directives. Ends with the distribution list of officials and project officers.

Target schedule for a Cuba project with three parts. A. Intelligence: NIE 85-62 on Cuba due 7 Feb; an interrogation operation at Opa Locka by 15 Feb with Defense, State, I&NS and FBI support; and a CIA survey of refugee points and inside Cuba with a capability report due 15 Feb. B. Political: 1960s tasks for toppling the regime covering political, economic (trade, shipping, nickel and food crops), and psychological (propaganda) measures, mostly due in February. E. Military: Defense contingency and special operations plans due 28 Feb; CIA sabotage schedule due 15 Feb; Defense support needs by 23 Feb; realistic task plans by 20 Feb; concern that the popular-movement framework could pretext armed intervention; distribution list.

summary: U.S. objective (1961): help Cubans overthrow the Communist regime via an internal popular revolt driven by a political action movement, backed by economic warfare, psychological operations, and sabotage/guerrilla groups, with Latin American support needed after the failed April 1961 operation. Covers the estimate of the situation (SNIE 85-61 error, NIE 85-62 delayed to 7 Feb), the initial phase (Nov 1961-Jan 1962: Lansdale mechanism, intelligence, political agents, OAS diplomacy, sugar/shipping sabotage, military contingencies, CIA shortfalls), and a target schedule for intelligence, political, and military tasks due February 1962.
